summary: A FlyDubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv issued squawk 7700 then 7500, diverted to Tabuk Saudi Arabia after an alleged attempt to crash the aircraft; Israeli passengers subdued the attacker. Israeli, Saudi, and Jordanian fighter jets scrambled. Iran raised readiness at 46 facilities amid fear of strikes. UK reports strong indications Iran linked to foiled attack on Fairford air base.
key_points: FlyDubai FZ1073 Dubai-Tel Aviv sent squawk 7700 then 7500, diverted to Tabuk Saudi Arabia after cockpit altercation; plane dropped 14,000 ft in under 30 seconds (Source: @manniefabian/59282).
Israeli security minister Katz: incident was thwarted jihadist attack; Israeli passengers broke into cockpit and subdued attacker (Source: @lelotsenzura/94409).
Israeli fighter jets scrambled toward the plane; Saudi and Jordanian jets also launched during the emergency (Source: @yediotnews25/135607).
Iran raised readiness at 46 facilities including oil, electricity, bridges, and airports fearing attack on infrastructure (Source: @New_security8200/204039).
UK PM says strong indications Iran linked to foiled attack on Fairford air base last weekend (Source: @mamlekate/104717).
Smoke columns observed from Qwaya, Erbil province, Iraq; black smoke from Ain Dar Saudi oil field near east-west pipeline (Source: @naya_foriraq/92183).
Saudi King Khalid airport air traffic stopped for third time this week (Source: @rodast_omiddana/81760).

sections.threat_assessment: The FlyDubai incident represents a potential new asymmetric tactic targeting civilian aviation on Dubai-Israel routes, with a jihadist attempting to crash the aircraft. The successful passenger intervention and simultaneous scrambling of Israeli, Saudi, and Jordanian fighters indicate elevated alert levels across the region. Combined with Iran raising readiness at 46 facilities and UK intelligence linking Iran to the Fairford air base attack, the threat environment for aviation and infrastructure has intensified significantly.
sections.regional_response: Israel has scrambled fighter jets and elevated security alerts following the FlyDubai incident. Saudi Arabia has halted air traffic at King Khalid airport for the third time this week. Iran has warned the UAE and raised facility readiness. The UK has publicly attributed the Fairford attack to Iran, signaling potential diplomatic and military consequences.
sections.intelligence_notes: Conflicting reports on the pilot's nationality (Emirati vs Russian) and attacker's origin (Omani vs unspecified) require verification. The sequence of squawk codes 7700 to 7500 suggests premeditation. The 'chain of survival' described by analysts—passengers subduing attacker, backup pilots taking controls—indicates extraordinary coordination. Iranian readiness at 46 facilities may precede a larger operation or be defensive posturing.
